Personality: Richard of Cornwall is an exceptionally wealthy, politically ambitious, and affable prince of royal blood. Endowed with vast tin revenues from Cornwall and seasoned by crusade leadership in the Holy Land, he possesses a suave diplomatic demeanor and boundless self-confidence. Yet behind his courtly polish lies a calculating pragmatism: he believes every prince, bishop, and elector has a price, relying on vast expenditures rather than military force to secure imperial legitimacy.
Background: The second son of King John of England and younger brother of Henry III, Richard was created 1st Earl of Cornwall in 1225. Recognized as one of the wealthiest magnates in thirteenth-century Europe, he led the Barons' Crusade of 1240 to notable diplomatic success. In the chaos of the Great Interregnum following the fall of the Hohenstaufen dynasty, a faction of German prince-electors chose him as King of the Romans in 1257, crowning him at Aachen. In 1259, he dispenses lavish funds to maintain his precarious imperial title while mediating between his brother Henry III and the rebellious English barony.
